lim: The review restricted its search to peer-reviewed journal articles from Google Scholar and PubMed with an average annual citation count of at least five, excluding grey literature and conference proceedings, which introduces certain limitations.

Inconsistent results across studies are probably caused by differences in diagnostic criteria, cohort size, disease duration, analytical techniques, and biological sample types, and many autoantibody findings originate from single research groups without independent replication.
Long-term cardiovascular outcomes in hEDS/HSD patients with hypertension remain poorly defined.

The authors note that high-quality large-scale randomized controlled trial evidence for gastric electrical stimulation, endoscopic interventions, and microbiota-targeted therapies remains limited, and DGAN-specific molecular biomarkers are still poorly defined.

Tilt-table testing may be limited by lack of availability and eligibility requirements, preventing some patients with clinically significant orthostatic intolerance from receiving a definitive diagnostic pathway.
Most of the reviewed studies were observational, which limits the robustness of the conclusions.

The authors note that mechanistic categories overlap with many patients having mixed physiology, and that evidence supporting secondary structural contributors (e.g., craniocervical/CSF-pressure disorders) is limited by referral bias and observational study design.

The review was not prospectively registered, included highly heterogeneous populations/interventions/outcome measures/timepoints across studies, and many included trials were small, single-center, or had infeasible blinding, limiting pooled quantitative conclusions.
The authors note there remains limited data on long COVID, dysautonomia, and the aetiology of POTS, and the impact of long COVID on future cardiac failure incidence remains unknown.

The authors note they did not observe synchronous network activity in the cultures and are unsure whether this reflects insufficient neuronal maturity or an inherent property of peripheral nervous system neurons, and they caution that gene expression patterns established in mouse DRG (e.g., ASIC fa…
Most of the reviewed studies were observational, which limits the robustness of the conclusions.

The authors note that direct comparisons among dopaminergic agents for OH risk are limited and often hampered by imprecise definitions of OH and OH-related symptoms, and that evidence for many pharmacological agents for supine/nocturnal hypertension derives from short-term or single-administration…

The review notes that many findings derive from small, single studies (e.g., cardiogenic vertigo literature limited to case reports) and that larger, more detailed studies are needed, particularly for vestibular syncope and OCHOs.

The authors note that current alpha-synuclein antibodies cannot reliably distinguish aggregate morphology, and that asyn seed amplification assay protocols vary widely in reaction conditions and replicate numbers between labs, complicating standardization, interpretation, and cross-study comparison…

The review notes that many findings derive from small, single studies (e.g., cardiogenic vertigo literature limited to case reports) and that larger, more detailed studies are needed, particularly for vestibular syncope and OCHOs.

The authors note that despite promising preclinical passive immunization results, clinical trials have so far failed to demonstrate efficacy, likely due to poor patient stratification, disease heterogeneity, and enrollment of patients in advanced disease stages.
The authors note that many early articles were either not accessible or written in languages other than English, limiting full inclusion in the review.

The article notes there is no consensus on the precise definition/classification of breathing pattern disorders and no gold-standard diagnostic test, and that high-quality data on effective management of some conditions (eg EILO) are currently lacking.

As a narrative review, no formal quality scoring tool or PRISMA flow diagram was applied, and observational study limitations such as self-report bias, diagnostic heterogeneity, and lack of randomized evidence were acknowledged.
Fatigue in MSA (and PD) lacks a universally accepted definition, classification, and measurement method, leading to widely discrepant prevalence estimates and making cross-study comparison difficult.
There is no effective treatment for any form of these conditions other than minimizing symptoms, indicating a gap the review does not resolve.

The review notes that despite extensive research the cause of dysautonomia across species remains elusive and likely multifactorial, and that some veterinary syndromes (e.g., ovine abomasal emptying defect, bovine FMD-associated signs) may not share the same underlying disease process as classical…

The single small RCT of IVIG in POTS is noted to have significant limitations and was likely underpowered, and the author notes that studies on pharmacotherapy for dysautonomia and associated systemic disorders are generally lacking.

This consensus statement reflects the opinion of experts in the field, but is not a formal evidence-based clinical guideline.

The authors note that immunologic assessment in POTS and dysautonomia has been extremely limited compared to ME/CFS and Long COVID, and that detailed studies on microglial activation in ME/CFS, POTS and dysautonomia are lacking.
The review notes that most cited studies are small, uncontrolled, or single-patient case reports, and that no randomised controlled trials of CoQ10 supplementation have yet been conducted in MSA.
This perspective piece focuses on mechanisms contributing to reduced CRF and acute exercise intolerance, explicitly excluding post-exertional malaise (PEM)-related conditions.
The authors note that the mechanism of POTS remains unknown and that it is unknown how many people worldwide suffer from long-COVID-19.
GWAS for POTS is particularly challenging due to the disorder's highly heterogeneous phenotype, which dilutes statistical power and complicates identification of consistent genetic associations.

Substantial heterogeneity in HRV acquisition protocols, recording durations, devices, and reported metrics across included studies precluded a pooled meta-analytic synthesis.
The etiology of POTS is largely unknown, reflecting a key limitation in current understanding of the condition.

The authors note a lack of long-term studies stratified by age group and coronavirus variant, limited data on differential effects of vaccine types, and inherent limitations of telemonitoring/AI tools (non-specificity of HRV changes, inability of AI to replace clinical judgment, and variable sensit…
The authors note that immune and targeted cancer therapies currently only have case-report evidence regarding autonomic dysfunction, leaving unanswered questions about prevalence and mechanism.

The authors note that high-quality large-scale randomized controlled trial evidence for gastric electrical stimulation, endoscopic interventions, and microbiota-targeted therapies remains limited, and DGAN-specific molecular biomarkers are still poorly defined.

As a narrative review, the paper acknowledges risks of selection and confirmation bias and states it does not allow for systematic methodological quality or publication bias assessment of the included studies.
The paper notes marked heterogeneity and intragroup variability among ME/CFS and Long-COVID patients, and that the referenced treatment-effectiveness study has its own limitations.

Most evidence on HRV in CLD comes from retrospective/observational studies with confounding by medications and comorbidities (e.g., type 2 diabetes mellitus), and there is no consensus on normal HRV cut-off values or standardized measurement protocols.

The platelet/cytokine study had low participant numbers, lacked case-controls, and assessed a restricted panel of cytokines/chemokines; the gAChR study may have recruitment bias from conference-based sampling; the IVIG case series was open-label with small sample size and reporting bias risk.

The authors note that prodromal features including autonomic dysfunction are individually nonspecific and acquire clinical relevance only within probabilistic frameworks or when integrated with biological markers, and that biomarkers of alpha-synuclein pathology currently support classification rat…

The authors acknowledge that detailed temporal studies linking microclots causally to POTS have not been conducted in animals (which may not be a good model), and that human SARS-CoV-2 challenge studies did not measure microclots.
